header: Date: 2027-11-02 | Time: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Product), Jared Lewis (Rivermark), Priya Nair (Rivermark), Marta Gomez (Rivermark), Leo Tran (Rivermark SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency benchmark results from last week's runs. Key focus: time-to-first-token (TTFT), streaming behavior, sequence-length effects, and kernel selection. Reviewed benchmark spreadsheet; identified two main sources of TTFT jitter (client TLS handshake and model kernel cold paths). Agreed on next experiments: kernel-switch runs on dedicated node, traffic sample for realistic sequences, and streaming buffer tuning. Action items assigned and follow-up demo scheduled.
topics: Kernel choices: cuBLAS vs Redwood custom kernel
Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for p95/p99
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll run 45 minutes ish, agenda is TTFT + streaming + kernel tests. quick intros.
[00:12] Jared Lewis: hi all, Jared here, lead ML eng at Rivermark. we're looking to hit sub-80ms TTFT for 512 tokens in our chat assistant, and p95 of overall response under 300ms.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Priya, infra, we'll share load profiles.
[00:31] Samira Khan: awesome, thanks. quick note - I uploaded the spreadsheet last night, link in chat, has raw traces and histogram tabs, caveat: some device names got munged by the collector so ignore exact GPU labels.
[00:48] Jordan Li: oh nice, saw that. question: are the traces from hosted or dedicated nodes?
[00:53] Samira Khan: mostly dedicated test nodes we spun up, one hosted run for baseline, the dedicated ones have the custom kernel enabled.
[01:05] Leo Tran: we noticed TTFT spikes around cold starts, like after short idle windows.
[01:12] Samira Khan: yeah that's one of the items - cold kernel path and JIT cost. we measured a ~120ms delta on first token in some runs. if you look at the TTFT breakdown tab, there's a TLS handshake column - client-side warmup was responsible for ~30ms in a few cases.
[01:32] Jared Lewis: hmm, 30ms from TLS is big for us, our client sdk does ephemeral connections frequently.
[01:39] Alex Park: ok so two levers: client connection reuse and server-side kernel warmup. for client reuse we suggested keep-alive and connection pooling, Jared, can you check if your SDK supports that?
[01:51] Jared Lewis: yes, it does, but it's not enabled by default. we can flip that in staging.
[01:56] Priya Nair: we'll schedule a quick patch to enable pooling.
[02:02] Samira Khan: on server side, we can pre-warm the kernel for hot model variants and pin a worker to maintain KV cache; that reduces cold-path jitter. the cost tradeoff is a little higher reserved capacity.
[02:15] Marta Gomez: cost is a concern, but p95 reliability is more important for customer-facing flows.
[02:21] Alex Park: understood. also we tested kernel choices - cuBLAS baseline vs Redwood custom kernel optimized for attention patterns. results: custom kernel gives better steady-state throughput and lower p99 for long sequences, but first-token time sometimes regresses if JIT is cold.
[02:40] Samira Khan: note: our custom kernel has a JIT compile step on first invocation for a given sequence length / batch shape. for repeated 512/8batch shapes it's fine, for varying lengths you may see extra latency.
[02:58] Jared Lewis: what's the mitigation there? can we pre-compile common sequence lengths?
[03:03] Samira Khan: yes, we can pre-warm and pre-compile using our deployment flags; Samira: I'll run a kernel-switch test: force cuBLAS vs custom and collect histograms - that'll show where we trade TTFT vs p99.
[03:18] Alex Park: perfect. also streaming - we saw some artifacts where small chunk sizes increased overall latency due to more round trips. in the sheet the streaming tab shows median token latency vs chunk size.
[03:32] Priya Nair: what's the recommended chunk size for our 50-200 token average responses?
[03:36] Samira Khan: for short responses (<=200 tokens) we recommend 64-token chunks with early flush at first token for TTFT, or if you need minimal p99, 128-token batching. it's a tradeoff.
[03:48] Jared Lewis: okay, so we try keep-alive + 64 chunk, see effect on TTFT.
[03:54] Alex Park: yes; also enable prefix caching for common prompts to cut generation tokens.
[03:59] Leo Tran: about sequence length distribution - our logs show 65% at 128 tokens, 25% at 512, 10% at 1024; is that pattern ok?
[04:11] Samira Khan: that helps - most traffic is short which favors our batching logic; the 10% long ones will drive p99, so we can route them to a heavier instance class or separate queue.
[04:23] Jordan Li: question - any regulatory constraints on routing? we prefer region-local inference.
[04:28] Alex Park: we can keep data in-region; routing policy supports region and tier-based routing.
[04:33] Marta Gomez: good. back to results - can you summarize the key numbers again?
[04:38] Samira Khan: sure, from the spreadsheet: baseline hosted run TTFT median ~60ms, dedicated custom kernel steady-state TTFT ~45ms, but first-token jitter up to 180ms on cold JIT samples. p95 steady-state for 512 tokens was ~260ms with custom kernel, cuBLAS was ~310ms.
[05:00] Jared Lewis: so custom kernel wins steady-state but hurts cold-start TTFT.
[05:05] Samira Khan: exactly. and streaming chunk tuning affects round-trip counts - smaller chunks increase overall tail slightly.
[05:13] Priya Nair: can we mitigate cold JIT by keeping a warm pool? what's the memory/cost impact?
[05:19] Samira Khan: warm pool of N pinned workers will increase reserved GPU hours; we estimate ~10% cost increase for a small pool but p99 drops by ~30-40ms. detailed numbers in cost tab.
[05:31] Alex Park: we should run the kernel-switch experiment on a dedicated node to get real histograms; Samira will do that. also Jared will flip client pooling in staging and run the sample load.
[05:44] Jared Lewis: one more thing - we saw some weird tokenization spikes with system prompts, maybe a tokenizer mismatch between model variants?
[05:51] Samira Khan: right, sometimes tokenizer config differs slightly between model forks; we'll confirm tokenization rules and ensure consistent bpe vocabulary.
[05:59] Jordan Li: can we add a quick regression test in CI for tokenization?
[06:03] Alex Park: yes, a small harness comparing token counts for canonical prompts - we have a repo we can share.
[06:10] Samira Khan: I'll link that in the follow-up.
[06:14] Marta Gomez: timeline - what's target for pilot completion?
[06:18] Alex Park: goal is to finish tuning and have a performance SLA proposal by end of November, ideally 2027-11-30.
[06:26] Priya Nair: sounds good.
[06:29] Samira Khan: nuts and bolts for experiments: I'll run kernel-switch (cuBLAS vs custom) on dedicated n1 with 512/8 batch shape, collect raw traces + histograms, upload to spreadsheet.
[06:42] Samira Khan: also I'll test pre-warming flags to see TTFT improvement.
[06:46] Jared Lewis: we'll enable client keep-alive and gather p50/p95 with our simulated load.
[06:52] Alex Park: ok, any blockers?
[06:55] Priya Nair: none immediate, just need the sample traffic file from Jared which he can export.
[07:01] Jared Lewis: I'll export it by Friday.
[07:04] Alex Park: great. quick recap - action items, deliverables, and follow-up demo week of 11/15. thanks all.
[07:12] Marta Gomez: thanks everyone.
[07:15] End of recording.
